briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. We will now begin the climate briefing for October 12, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Global Temperature Rise and Warnings of Extreme Weather
sections.content: According to the Copernicus Climate Change Service, last September was the second warmest on record, with global average temperatures remaining above 1.5°C [89, 107]. Notably, there have been warnings that this year, 2026, could become the hottest year on record due to a super El Niño phenomenon [108]. In Sydney, a total fire ban has already been imposed due to the risk of bushfires caused by high temperatures and dry lightning, with temperatures exceeding 35.2°C recorded [115]. Domestically, heat-related deaths this summer increased by 24% compared to the previous year, with a significant rise in fatalities among the elderly aged 80 and above, highlighting the direct health threats posed by climate change [85]. Evidence of global warming caused by human activities is becoming clearer than ever before [95].

sections.title: ⚠️ The Shadow of Climate Change Cast Across Ecosystems and Society
sections.content: Climate change is having widespread impacts across our ecosystems and society. In the waters off Geomun Island in the South Sea, previously unseen marine species, including 'Bukang-i,' have appeared, interpreted as warning signs sent by climate change [2, 4, 10]. 75% of global surfing spots are now in a 'high-risk' state due to climate change and coastal development, with new research pointing out that surfing destinations worldwide are increasingly vulnerable to climate change [3, 7, 105]. In Afghanistan, wildlife is facing extinction due to climate change and habitat destruction [98], and rainforest restoration efforts in Scotland are becoming more complex because of climate change [106]. Climate change also affects daily life, such as the suspension of sports events [110], and it has been re-emphasized that the climate crisis and air pollution are closely intertwined issues that cannot be solved separately [5].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Carbon Neutrality Efforts and Current Challenges
sections.content: Domestically, various efforts are continuing to achieve carbon neutrality goals. Suwon City hosted its 2nd Carbon Neutrality Festival, emphasizing citizen participation and action [21, 22, 35, 43], and the Suwon City Council also shared its efforts to create a carbon-neutral city with its citizens [36, 38, 53, 55, 68, 73]. Yeosu City held a National Assembly Carbon Neutrality Forum to attract COP33, fostering consensus and seeking cooperation [19, 26, 29, 30, 44, 62, 66, 69]. Meanwhile, Incheon City's greenhouse gas reduction performance increased by 22% compared to the previous year, receiving positive evaluations for accelerating its '2045 Carbon Neutrality' implementation [20, 40, 47, 50, 52, 60, 64, 65, 67, 70, 71, 72]. However, there were also conflicting reports indicating that performance was below target for two consecutive years [54]. Challenges remain, such as the argument that hydrogen reduction steel, a core technology for achieving carbon neutrality, is difficult without nuclear power generation, and the dilemma between energy saving in pharmaceutical factories and compliance with GMP regulations [28, 33].

sections.title: 🌱 Renewable Energy Expansion and Climate Adaptation Technology Development
sections.content: News of renewable energy expansion and adaptation technology development to combat climate change has also been reported. Household solar power facilities will now be eligible for renewable energy certificates, which is expected to contribute to the wider adoption of renewable energy [84]. Samsung Electro-Mechanics is pursuing a 30% transition to renewable energy and linking it with ESG performance [76]. Samsung C&T has launched a large-scale energy storage system (BESS) project worth 210 billion KRW in Australia, accelerating its expansion into new and renewable energy [78]. Domestically, KMI and Chonnam National University are jointly researching aquaculture technologies and systems for climate change response [8], and Goesan County is modernizing its seed potato production infrastructure to adapt to climate change and increase farm household income [12]. Furthermore, Vietnam is enhancing cooperation with Italy in health and climate change response [14], and a climate crisis adaptation forum was held in the Gwangju-Jeonnam Integrated Special City to find solutions for extreme weather conditions [15].

sections.title: 🌍 International Policy Coordination and Research Cooperation
sections.content: The international community continues its policy and academic efforts to address climate change. The EU is pursuing plans to accelerate CO2 reduction through the COP31 climate agreement, and arguments have been made for the necessity of coordinating monetary and fiscal policies in response to climate change [90, 91]. The Council has set the EU's position ahead of the upcoming Climate Change and Biodiversity Summit [94], and Türkiye plans to host an international climate media tour in anticipation of the UN Climate Change Conference [100]. Furthermore, The Lancet warned of 17 global health threats, including climate change, emphasizing the importance of a multifaceted approach [113]. In the academic field, research achievements are being recognized, such as a sociologist alumnus researching climate change receiving a MacArthur Fellowship [88].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has once again confirmed the severe impacts of climate change and demonstrated that various domestic and international efforts are simultaneously underway to address them. This is a critical time when sustained attention and action are becoming even more important. This concludes the daily climate briefing for October 12, 2026.
